intended_object: For a category C with a shift by an additive monoid M, a class of morphisms W and objects X, Y, this is the smallness condition saying that for all a, b ∈ M the Hom-set from X[a] to Y[b] in the localized category C[W⁻¹] is w-small. Taken from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body says exactly this: for all a and b in M, `HasSmallLocalizedHom.{w} W (X⟦a⟧) (Y⟦b⟧)` holds, i.e. the Hom-type from X⟦a⟧ to Y⟦b⟧ in the localization is w-small. Here the shifts are taken in C, before localizing. The lemma `hasSmallLocalizedShiftedHom_iff` right after the definition shows that this is equivalent to the version with the shifts taken in D. It needs a localization functor L that commutes with the shift, which is the expected compatibility.

This is a set-theoretic smallness condition used to build the types `SmallShiftedHom`. It is a genuine, well-defined property at its natural generality: any additive monoid M, any category with a shift, any W. It is stated through Mathlib's general `HasSmallLocalizedHom`, and Mathlib has no other declaration of this notion. Nothing is missing and nothing is overly specialized.
